question: How much additional whole-application speed can be obtained by deliberately cheaper generated hydraulic tables while retaining hydrologically relevant accuracy?

frozen_baseline.coordinate: log-spaced raw negative pressure head from -1e7 cm to the K-saturation branch, plus saturated endpoint
frozen_baseline.whole_hupsel_F5_note: Only two printed signed-zero balance-deviation fields differ under the strict historical text-identity gate; this is not the acceptance metric for this research workunit.

hypotheses.H1: The 400-row representation is over-resolved for practical hydrological fidelity.
hypotheses.H2: Reducing row count lowers lookup and cache cost enough to increase whole-Hupsel speed beyond the 400-row baseline.
hypotheses.H3: A non-uniform purpose-aware grid can dominate a same-size naive log grid on the speed-accuracy frontier.

phase_1.purpose: isolate row-count effect before changing interpolation family or node-placement algorithm
fixed: same wet continuation and saturation handling
same solver, timestep, retry and tolerance policies

accuracy_metrics.signed_zero_policy: Signed zero is compared numerically as zero for TAB-SPEED-ACCURACY only. This does not amend or supersede the frozen F-TAB02-F historical preservation contract.

performance_metrics.claim_policy: No minimum speed is assumed prospectively; report measured frontier.

decision_rule: Do not choose a winner before measurements. Identify Pareto-nondominated variants by measured runtime and hydrological error. Only after Phase 1 may a purpose-aware/non-uniform grid be designed prospectively.
production_effect: NONE. Research branch only; no canonical admission or F-TAB02-F normalization change.
